title: Algebraization of a formal glueing datum
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $t\in\mathbf N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(t)\to R$, and $I=(f_i)_i$, and suppose $R/I\to S/IS$ is bijective. Let $\mathrm{Can}:\mathrm{Mod}_R\to\mathrm{Glue}(\varphi,f)$ be a functor whose object at every $M$ has prime module $S\otimes_R M$, chart modules $M_{f_i}$, and actual canonical structural maps $c^M_{f_i},\sigma^M_{f_i,f_j}$, identified by bundled equalities and heterogeneous equalities [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. For every glueing datum $X$ there exists an $R$-module $E$ and an isomorphism $\mathrm{Can}(E)\cong X$. This asserts only essential surjectivity, with no assumption on Can on morphisms and no assertion about its Hom maps.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER, second and third paragraphs of the proof; steps 7–11 of prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence.

proof.text: (Part (2): the module $H^0(\mathbf M)$ and the morphism $\Psi$.) Let $\mathbf M=(M',(M_i),(\alpha_i),(\alpha_{ij}))$ be an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$. Let $H=H^0(\mathbf M)\subseteq M'\times\prod_iM_i$ be the $R$-module of the families $(m',(m_i))$ with $\alpha_i(m'/1)=m_i\otimes1$ and $\alpha_{ij}(m_i/1)=m_j/1$ for all $i,j$, with projections $p':H\to M'$ and $p_i:H\to M_i$ (Remark 05EL). By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0-localization] there is for each $i$ a unique $R$-linear $\Psi_i:H_{f_i}\to M_i$ with $\Psi_i(h/1)=p_i(h)$, and it is bijective; as $f_i$ acts bijectively on $M_i$, $\Psi_i(h/f_i^e)=f_i^{-e}p_i(h)$. Let $\Psi':H\otimes_RS\to M'$ be the $S$-linear map with $\Psi'(h\otimes s)=s\,p'(h)$ (well defined since $(h,s)\mapsto s\,p'(h)$ is $R$-bilinear [def-weil-module-base-change]). Then $\Psi=(\Psi',(\Psi_i)_i):\mathrm{Can}(H)\to\mathbf M$ is a morphism of $\mathrm{Glue}$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: (i) $\alpha_i\circ\Psi'_{f_i}=(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$, since on $(h\otimes s)/f_i^e$ the left side is $\alpha_i(s\,p'(h)/f_i^e)=s f_i^{-e}\alpha_i(p'(h)/1)=sf_i^{-e}(p_i(h)\otimes1)$ ($\alpha_i$ is $S$-linear and $R$-linear) and the right side is $(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)((h/f_i^e)\otimes s)=f_i^{-e}p_i(h)\otimes s$, the same element; (ii) $\alpha_{ij}\circ(\Psi_i)_{f_j}=(\Psi_j)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^H_{f_i,f_j}$, since on $(h/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ the left side is $\alpha_{ij}((f_i^{-a}p_i(h))/f_j^b)=f_i^{-a}f_j^{-b}\alpha_{ij}(p_i(h)/1)=f_i^{-a}f_j^{-b}(p_j(h)/1)$ and the right side is $(\Psi_j)_{f_i}((h/f_j^b)/f_i^a)=(f_j^{-b}p_j(h))/f_i^a$, the same element ($\alpha_{ij}$ is $R$-linear between modules on which $f_i,f_j$ act bijectively, so it commutes with their inverses). These elements generate the sources additively (step 1), using the formulas for $c$ and $\sigma$ [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps].

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813), proof, first paragraph (the natural morphism Psi); H^0 from Remark 05EL (line 24641)

proof.text: (Part (2): $\Psi'$ has $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel.) By (i) of step 7, $\Psi'_{f_i}=\alpha_i^{-1}\circ(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$, a composite of isomorphisms ($\alpha_i$ by [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], $c^H_{f_i}$ by step 1, $\Psi_i\otimes_RS$ with inverse $\Psi_i^{-1}\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]). Let $K=\operatorname{Ker}\Psi'$ and $Q=\operatorname{Coker}\Psi'$, $S$-modules. Localizing the exact sequences of $R$-modules $0\to K\to H\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\Psi'}M'$ and $H\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\Psi'}M'\to Q\to0$ at $\{1,f_i,f_i^2,\dots\}$ gives exact sequences [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] in which $\Psi'_{f_i}$ is bijective, so $K_{f_i}=0$ and $Q_{f_i}=0$. For $x\in K$ (or $Q$), $x/1=0$ in $K_{f_i}$ gives $e_i$ with $f_i^{e_i}x=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]; with $e=e_1+\dots+e_t$ every monomial $f_1^{a_1}\cdots f_t^{a_t}$ with $\sum a_k=e$ has some $a_k\ge e_k$, and these monomials generate $I^e$, so $I^ex=0$. Hence $K$ and $Q$ are $I$-power torsion.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813), proof, second paragraph (kernel and cokernel of Psi are of the form (K,0,0,0), (Q,0,0,0))

proof.text: (Part (2): $\Psi'$ is injective.) Let $y\in K$. Then $y\in(H\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ (step 8), and since $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ is finitely generated, $\varphi$ is flat and $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, there is $h\in H[I^\infty]$ with $h\otimes1=y$ [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-submodule-flat-base-change-iso]. Then $p'(h)=\Psi'(h\otimes1)=0$. If $I^nh=0$ then $f_i^nh=0$, so $h/1=0$ in $H_{f_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] and $p_i(h)=\Psi_i(h/1)=0$ for every $i$. As $h=(p'(h),(p_i(h))_i)$ in $M'\times\prod_iM_i$, $h=0$ and $y=0$. So $K=0$. (The source argues with $H^0((K,0,0,0))=K$, left exactness of $H^0$ and bijectivity of $H^0(\Psi)$; the computation here is that argument written out.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813), proof, second paragraph (K = 0)

proof.text: (Part (2): the extension.) The $S$-module $Q$ is $I$-power torsion as an $R$-module (step 8), so $\varepsilon:Q\to Q\otimes_RS$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, is bijective [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-module-flat-base-change-iso]. It is $S$-linear: the map $\mu:Q\otimes_RS\to Q$, $x\otimes s\mapsto sx$, is well defined and $S$-linear ($(x,s)\mapsto sx$ is $R$-bilinear [def-weil-module-base-change]), and $\mu\circ\varepsilon=\mathrm{id}_Q$, so $\mu=\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon=\mu^{-1}$ is $S$-linear. With $\rho:M'\to Q$ the cokernel map, $\pi=\varepsilon\circ\rho$ gives, by steps 8 and 9, an exact sequence of $S$-modules $0\to H\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{\Psi'}M'\xrightarrow{\pi}Q\otimes_RS\to0$ (this is the source's 'we may think of $Q$ as an $R$-module which is $I$-power torsion so that $Q=Q\otimes_RS$'). By [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-extension-flat-descent] (with $N=H$, $\iota=\Psi'$) there are an $R$-module $E$, an exact sequence $0\to H\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$ of $R$-modules and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\theta:E\otimes_RS\to M'$ with $\theta\circ(j\otimes_RS)=\Psi'$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence, line 24813), proof, third paragraph (Lemma 05EH, dualizing-lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, gives E)

proof.text: (Part (2): $\mathrm{Can}(E)\cong\mathbf M$; essential surjectivity.) Since $Q$ is $I$-power torsion, $Q_{f_i}=0$ (each $x\in Q$ has $f_i^nx=0$ for some $n$, so $x/f_i^e=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]); localizing $0\to H\to E\to Q\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] shows that $j_{f_i}:H_{f_i}\to E_{f_i}$ is bijective, and then so are $(j_{f_i})_{f_k}$ and $(j\otimes_RS)_{f_i}=(c^E_{f_i})^{-1}\circ(j_{f_i}\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$ (naturality of $c$, step 2). Put $\Phi_i=\Psi_i\circ j_{f_i}^{-1}:E_{f_i}\to M_i$, an $R$-linear bijection (step 7), and $\Phi=(\theta,(\Phi_i)_i)$. $\Phi:\mathrm{Can}(E)\to\mathbf M$ is a morphism [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]: (i) precomposed with the bijection $(j\otimes_RS)_{f_i}$, $\alpha_i\circ\theta_{f_i}$ becomes $\alpha_i\circ(\theta\circ(j\otimes_RS))_{f_i}=\alpha_i\circ\Psi'_{f_i}=(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$ (step 7) and $(\Phi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^E_{f_i}$ becomes $(\Phi_i\otimes_RS)\circ(j_{f_i}\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}=(\Psi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^H_{f_i}$ (step 2 and functoriality of $-\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]), so $\alpha_i\circ\theta_{f_i}=(\Phi_i\otimes_RS)\circ c^E_{f_i}$; (ii) precomposed with the bijection $(j_{f_i})_{f_k}$, $\alpha_{ik}\circ(\Phi_i)_{f_k}$ becomes $\alpha_{ik}\circ(\Psi_i)_{f_k}=(\Psi_k)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^H_{f_i,f_k}$ (step 7) and $(\Phi_k)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^E_{f_i,f_k}$ becomes $(\Phi_k)_{f_i}\circ(j_{f_k})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^H_{f_i,f_k}=(\Psi_k)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^H_{f_i,f_k}$ (step 2; localization respects composition [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (1)), so they are equal. All components of $\Phi$ are bijective, and the family of inverses $(\theta^{-1},(\Phi_i^{-1}))$ is a morphism $\mathbf M\to\mathrm{Can}(E)$ (compose the two relations with the inverses on both sides; $(\Phi_i^{-1})_{f_k}=((\Phi_i)_{f_k})^{-1}$ and $\Phi_i^{-1}\otimes_RS=(\Phi_i\otimes_RS)^{-1}$ by functoriality), inverse to $\Phi$ since composition is componentwise. So $\mathbf M\cong\mathrm{Can}(E)$, and $\mathrm{Can}$ is essentially surjective. With step 6, $\mathrm{Can}$ is an equivalence (fully faithful and essentially surjective), which is (2). (A posteriori $Q=0$, as the source remarks; it is not needed.)

lean.statement:
theorem canonical_essentially_surjective {R : Type u} {S : Type v}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (φ : R →+* S) (t : ℕ) (f : Fin t → R)
    (Can : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R ⥤ Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f)
    (hobj : (∀ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R,
        (Can.obj M).M' = extend φ M ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, (Can.obj M).M i =
          ModuleCat.of (Localization.Away (f i)) (LocalizedModule.Away (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i : Fin t, HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha i).toLinearMap (compare φ (f i) M)) ∧
        (∀ i j : Fin t,
          HEq ((Can.obj M).alpha_overlap i j).toLinearMap (swap (f i) (f j) M))))
    (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap ((Ideal.span (Set.range f)).map φ) φ Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (X : Data.{u, v, max u v w} φ f) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max u v w} R, Nonempty (Can.obj M ≅ X)
